text:
COP climbed 0.9% today to $136.82, rebounding modestly after a rough two weeks that saw the stock drop 8.2%. The timing aligns with tentative optimism around Iran tensions easing—Trump signaled Monday that the conflict could end "fairly soon," which briefly pushed Brent crude below $90 a barrel for the first time since August. Oil prices matter directly to ConocoPhillips' earnings, and any relief from geopolitical risk typically lifts energy stocks, even if the move remains fragile given the gap between US oil (trading at $99.64) and global prices (Brent at $107.03).

The broader picture is one of whipsaw volatility in oil markets. The two-week slide likely reflects investor uncertainty about whether Iran tensions will actually ease or whether they'll re-escalate, creating real swings in crude prices and therefore in energy company valuations. Today's small bounce suggests a brief relief rally, but without a concrete deal, the stock could easily reverse again if the geopolitical picture darkens.
